headline: High-risk filesystem and clipboard interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the local machine while ai-engineering-hub has no isolation or runtime protections documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can ingest clipboard/files and execute instructions from local content, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent/MCP/RAG hub with no documented isolation or provenance controls. A shared filesystem or clipboard bridge could let attacker-controlled content steer Open Interpreter. The pathway is plausible, but not proven by direct pairwise evidence.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub writes attacker-controlled text to a shared file or clipboard that Open Interpreter reads
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent reduced confirmation
IF the pair is connected through a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require human review before Open Interpreter executes any file-derived instruction
Run Open Interpreter without auto_run
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter has broad filesystem access and can transmit context to configured model providers, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent hub with no documented data-loss controls. If sensitive local files are reachable, Open Interpreter can expose them through prompts or outputs. The pairwise leakage path is stronger than for A because B explicitly touches the entire local machine.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is pointed at a directory containing secrets or regulated data
IF model-provider API keys are configured for Open Interpreter
IF ai-engineering-hub forwards local content into Open Interpreter without redaction
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a non-sensitive directory
Remove or rotate model-provider API keys before testing
Separate the agents onto different OS accounts
Disable clipboard transfer of sensitive text
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. ai-engineering-hub is an agent hub that may also orchestrate file-based workflows, so overlapping writes can race or corrupt shared artifacts. Because both sides can plausibly touch the same workspace, the conflict risk is material in default local setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory
IF either agent modifies git state without external locking
IF ai-engineering-hub emits files that Open Interpreter edits in place
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Serialize access with a lock file
Avoid concurrent git operations
Make one agent read-only for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can take actions from generated text, and ai-engineering-hub is an agent-oriented repository that may produce instructions or artifacts consumed downstream. If Open Interpreter treats those outputs as authoritative, a mistaken upstream result can cascade into incorrect local actions. The blast radius is broader than a single document but still bounded by local execution.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub output is fed directly into Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to execute without per-step human verification
IF downstream tasks include file edits or shell commands
mitigations: Insert a verification step before execution
Require human approval for each generated command
Limit Open Interpreter to dry-run mode
Keep upstream outputs as plain text, not executable instructions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can handle model-provider API keys, while ai-engineering-hub is an open-source agent hub with no documented residency or retention controls. If regulated data is present on the host, the pair can move it into a third-party model workflow without clear compliance boundaries. The other agent is not separately cited because the compliance issue is driven by Open Interpreter's local-machine reach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored on the same host Open Interpreter can access
IF Open Interpreter sends prompts to a third-party model provider
IF no DPA, retention, or residency controls are configured
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the host
Use a provider with approved residency and retention terms
Rotate any exposed API keys
Run Open Interpreter only on sanitized test data
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy
